# MD-C11 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (2024) Evaluation of the Housing First Pilots: Final synthesis report. October 2024. Report by ICF (consortium with Bryson Purdon Social Research, Matt Rayment Consulting, Homeless Link and Heriot-Watt University) for MHCLG. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/housing-first-pilot-national-evaluation-reports

Title page check (PDF p.1): "Evaluation of the Housing First Pilots / Final synthesis report / October 2024 / Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government". No individual authors are named; the consortium is named on p.12 (PDF 16). The reference given in the brief ("Housing First pilots: National evaluation, final synthesis report") is the gov.uk collection title, not the document title.

Proposal: eligible.

Page references give the report pagination first and the PDF page in brackets (arabic page n = PDF n+4).

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- The object is the three Housing First Pilots (Greater Manchester, Liverpool City Region, West Midlands combined authorities), funded by a £28 million government commitment (Autumn 2017 Budget) plus a £13.9 million extension (p.4, PDF 8; p.13, PDF 17; Table 5.1-5.2, p.50, PDF 54).
- The relationships studied are those between clients and support workers (s.4.4, p.41-42, PDF 45-46) and between the Pilots and housing providers, health, social care and criminal justice services (s.4.3, s.4.6, p.38-45, PDF 42-49).

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: baseline (n=312), 6-month (n=159) and 12-month (n=167) client surveys with significance tests (Chapter 3, p.23-30, PDF 27-34); staff-reported three-year outcomes (s.3.3, p.30-33); monitoring information (s.4.2-4.3, p.36-38); cost-benefit analysis (Chapter 5, p.49-59).
- Qualitative: four rounds of interviews and focus groups, 313 interviews including 81 service users (Table 1.1, p.16, PDF 20); 72 fidelity interviews (p.16); qualitative findings in s.2.9 (p.21), s.3.4 (p.33-34) and Chapter 4.

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.

## Points for A1
- Delivery is by combined authorities, local authorities and commissioned voluntary-sector providers under central government funding; read as publicly funded.
- The report is a synthesis of earlier published reports (process, 12-month outcomes, CBA) and unpublished fidelity assessments. Some executive summary figures are not reported in the synthesis body (see extraction notes); the register is limited to this document.
